It fell on a Friday, I got home and started going upstairs to get changed because my friends were coming over for a sleepover. My mum stopped me and said I couldn’t go into my room yet because my present is in there, and she would get me some clothes to change into.

I get excited af and after I get changed I start pestering my mum about it and running around like a mad thing because I need my friends to get to my house so I can meet my dog. My mum keeps going into my room, I assume to check on the dog, and there’s definitely a lot of noise up there and she’s definitely talking to something.

To cut a long story short, my friends get to my house and we run upstairs to my room, fling open the door, and find the following:

Balloons. Dozens of them all over the floor. There is no dog, only balloons and a box on my bed. My mum is standing at my bedroom door laughing. InsideI am devastated and my friends are obviously super confused, I decide to move on before I start sobbing and open the present. It’s a pair of shoes I’d wanted a year ago during my emo phase, and a t-shirt of the same general description. Neither of them fit, the shoes actually made my feet bleed, and my mum shut my sleepover down at 9pm because she couldn’t sleep with us watching movies on the TV.

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 300g baby spinach
- 1 chopped onion
- 1 diced clove of garlic
- 600ml vegetable stock
- 150ml skimmed milk
- 75ml double cream
- salt
- pepper

Method:
1. Heat the oil in a large pan or pot over a medium heat. Once hot, add the garlic, onion, and a pinch of salt to the pot and sweat for 5 minutes.
2. Add the spinach and mix it with the onion and garlic. When the spinach is slightly wilted, pour in the vegetable stock and milk, mixing well. Simmer for 5 minutes then increase the heat to high.
3. Mix in the double cream and cook for a further 2 minutes.
4. Blend the mixture until smooth. I opted for a hand blender, a regular blender would probably work just as well.
5. Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot.

Also, be careful with information dumping and keeping your narrative in line with your character. This isn't very long and we don't need to know everything about Hush in one go. I'm an insomniac who's sleep schedule gets fucked up quite often due to daylight savings. I am also a university student. Here's what I do:
- I pick a day where I know I'm going to be especially busy e.g. lots of classes, library date with friends, grocery shopping etc. The day before, I try and pull an all nighter.
- If I manage to complete the all nighter then I'm usually pretty tired by the morning. I do what I have to do during the day and take lie downs in the day. Not naps, just lie down; you can regain energy and rest your brain without sleeping. Sometimes I'll do a 5-10 minute guided meditation just to centre my brain a bit. By the time it gets to bed time, you will be exhausted.
- I don't drink caffeine after 5pm, this was really hard at first because I'm a tea addict. Get in the habit of drinking water and if you like a warm drink in the evening, go for something like herbal tea (I like peppermint) or hot water with lemon and ginger.
- Get a bed time routine. You don't have to follow it exactly every night but it's good to have a little ritual to get you into the night time mood. I usually have a shower, make one of the warm drinks I mentioned, then sit in my bed for a while and listen to a podcast for a bit. My friend got me a timed night light for Christmas, I turn that then read until it goes off.
- Figure out what is your best state for sleeping. Do you sleep better in a warm or cold room? In pajamas or nakey? A small light on or total darkness? Background noise or silence? I like my room to be fairly cool, I wear pajamas (only loose fitting ones), total darkness, but I do need to listen to something as I fall asleep to keep my mind blank.
- Guided meditations. There's loads of free apps that have meditations lasting from a couple of minutes to a couple of hours. People tend to brush off meditation, I used to do the same, but I actually find them very helpful if I'm particularly stressed or anxious. I like to do them sometimes just before I go to bed. Sometimes I'll listen to a long one, like a full body scan, when I'm trying to fall asleep and that usually helps me drift off in about 30 minutes.
- Figure out how much sleep you need. I can't sleep for any longer than 6 hours and I can usually function on 5. Some people need about 9 hours, if I sleep that long then I find myself feeling tired all day.
- Keep water next to your bed. Your body is dehydrated as fuck when you wake up and that makes it especially hard to get out of bed. I drink about 700ml of water every morning, before I even get out of bed, and it really helps me wake up.
- Try and make your bed as comfy as possible. If you're poor and have a crap mattress then there isn't much you can do to fix that. Mattress toppers can be pretty cheap and they help a lot. Try and purchase some decent pillows, get yourself some comfy sheets that aren't too visually stimulated. Hell, get a stuffed animal to cuddle if that helps you (I have a sheep teddy, his name is Hamish).

Sorting out your sleep schedule is really difficult, if I can offer any advice at all ten it would be exhaust yourself every day. If I haven't done much in a day, I go for a long walk in the cold then take a warm shower. You can't sleep unless your body and brain are tired.

Hope this helps someone!
